article_title: Modelling Human Teaching Tactics and Strategies for Tutoring Systems: 14 Years On
citation: Benedict du Boulay & Rosemary Luckin. (2015). Modelling Human Teaching Tactics and Strategies for Tutoring Systems: 14 Years On. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-015-0053-0
title: Akhras and Self's four properties of constructivist learning interaction sequences
description: Under Akhras and Self's view of Constructivism, teaching emphasises "the process rather than the product of learning", and intelligent learning environments evaluate learning according to four properties of constructivist learning processes: cumulativeness, constructiveness, self-regulatedness, and reflectiveness. These properties describe sequences of learning interactions and inform decisions about the learning opportunities provided to learners, taking into account the affordances of learning situations. The review presents this as an example of teaching strategies derived from epistemological learning theories.
requirements: Learning environments must be able to evaluate learning interactions according to the four properties to make decisions about learning opportunities
constraints: The framework is presented as one constructivist view among several overlapping theory-derived strategies in the review
target_learning_goals: constructivist learning processes including self-regulation and reflection
examples: Cumulativeness involves the same entity being experienced more than once in a sequence; constructiveness involves entities experienced earlier being related to new entities the learner generates later
key_sources: Benedict du Boulay & Rosemary Luckin. (2015). Modelling Human Teaching Tactics and Strategies for Tutoring Systems: 14 Years On. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-015-0053-0

article_title: The Design and Implementation of the Akamai Maui Short Course
citation: Ryan Montgomery, Dave Harrington, Sarah Sonnett, Mark Pitts, Isar Mostafanezhad, Mike Foley, Eddie Laag, and Lisa Hunter. (2010). The Design and Implementation of the Akamai Maui Short Course. ASP Conference Series. https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.4458
title: Akamai Maui Short Course: one-week inquiry-based internship preparation course
description: The AMSC is the first week of the eight-week Akamai Internship Program, which places Hawaii college students in Maui high-tech internships and aims to "retain and advance students in science and engineering ﬁelds, and to create a local technical workforce". The course contains four sequential full inquiry activities (Camera Obscura and Sun Shadows, Lenses and Refraction, Color and Light, and the Adaptive Optics Demonstrator) plus Communication and Science, Technology and Society strands, tailored to host-site needs, with a printed day-by-day schedule (Table 1).
requirements: Instructors trained in inquiry design (via the PDP)
Host-site employer input to tailor goals
Low-cost optics materials and an AO workstation
constraints: Small Maui academic community means some students arrive with prior exposure to the same inquiry activities, creating redundancy
target_learners: freshmen and sophomore community-college students from underrepresented groups in Hawaii
target_learning_goals: science and engineering process skills, optics content, communication and professional skills for internship success
examples: The 2009 course ran five days from an opening session through the Adaptive Optics Workstation activity, mentor-strategies session, and post-knowledge survey.
key_sources: Ryan Montgomery, Dave Harrington, Sarah Sonnett, Mark Pitts, Isar Mostafanezhad, Mike Foley, Eddie Laag, and Lisa Hunter. (2010). The Design and Implementation of the Akamai Maui Short Course. ASP Conference Series. https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.4458
